errors.text: The proposed temperature and strain-rate regime (673–873 K and 10^-3–10^-1 s^-1) does not reconstruct the molecular-dynamics regime of 10–600 K and 10^8–10^10 s^-1.
The hypothesis replaces vacancy-assisted Shockley-partial nucleation and stacking-fault formation with an unsupported pile-up, super-jog, climb, and dynamic-recovery mechanism.
It assumes moderate-to-high stacking-fault energy, whereas the target deformation involves extensive intrinsic and extrinsic stacking faults generated by 1/6<112> Shockley partials.
The cited evidence concerns materially different refractory or duplex alloys and does not establish strain-rate-insensitive yielding in single-crystal FCC FeNiCrMn.
The falsification rule treats detection of HCP material as evidence of martensitic transformation, so it would incorrectly reject HCP-like local coordination produced by ordinary FCC stacking faults.
